nodes.label: Verification Method (three accepted proofs)
nodes.rationale: A source counts as verified only if its publisher returned the record over HTTPS, its file was downloaded and measured, or its metadata was read from a machine-readable API; snippets, reposts, memory, inferred values, and color-picked pixels are rejected as evidence.

nodes.label: Three Distinct Layers (scientific / rendered / derived)
nodes.rationale: The layers must not be collapsed into a single 'NASA data' label; otherwise a customer-facing claim would conflate a model-observation synthesis, NASA's render, and any later processing.

nodes.label: NASA SVS Record 3912 (verified fields)
nodes.rationale: Verified directly from the page API so the interface can cite title, release, credits, datasets, and 2007-03-25 to 2008-03-03 coverage without inventing anything.

nodes.label: Bundled Still Is Frame 25000 (19 June 2007)
nodes.source_location: 4 The bundled still is a single frame
nodes.rationale: NASA's frame-timestamp file maps frame 25000 to 2007-06-19T12:00:00Z, so the still is one instant rather than a temporal composite; the distinction is surfaced in the plate caption. The API filename's '2028x1024' is treated as a publisher typo because measured pixels and structured metadata say 2048 x 1024.

nodes.label: ECCO2 / ECCO Cube92 Legacy Product
nodes.rationale: A model-observation synthesis on a cube-sphere grid at 18-30 km with 50 vertical levels, fitted to observations by least squares; it is not a direct measurement at every grid point, and its native cube-sphere grid is not a simple latitude-longitude image a browser can treat as one.

nodes.label: Open Question: Exact 2012 ECCO2 Release
nodes.rationale: The SVS record names ECCO2 and MITgcm but not the run identifier, build date, forcing set, or checksums; because the render was released in 2012 it likely used an older run than the currently listed Cube92, but that is an inference recorded as a question, not asserted in the interface.

nodes.label: Numerical ECCO2 Access Blockers
nodes.rationale: No anonymous numerical endpoint was verified, PO.DAAC requires Earthdata authentication (credentials must never reach the browser), the current product is terabytes across hundreds of thousands of granules, the 2012 release is unnamed, and the cube-sphere grid does not map to an image.

nodes.label: ECCO V4r4 Is Not a Substitute for the Render's Source
nodes.source_location: 6 Current ECCO distribution is not a substitute
nodes.rationale: Downloading V4r4 (1992-2018, >3 TB, ~90 products on 0.5 degree and llc90 grids) and treating it as 'the data behind the image' would be a provenance error, so the project does not do this.

nodes.label: Rule: Color Picking Is Not Data Extraction
nodes.source_location: 5 What the image can and cannot support / 11 Rules for future data work
nodes.rationale: Compositing and antialiasing alter color and no validated per-pixel legend exists, so pixel sampling would convert a rendering choice into invented data; the colorbar variant was therefore not bundled or transcribed.

nodes.label: Eight Rules for Future Data Work
nodes.rationale: Never infer a measurement from a rendered image, keep provenance labels distinct, name the release, measure the asset (bytes/checksum/query/date), keep credentials server-side, state any release mismatch in the interface, use null rather than zero for missing samples, and label synthetic fixtures in the UI.

nodes.label: Licensing and Attribution (NASA public domain, ECCO citation, OFL, ISC)
nodes.rationale: NASA SVS content is public domain unless noted and only one rendered still is used, but media guidelines still imply no endorsement, so the project credits the publisher and scientists and states it is not an official NASA product.
